A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pfaffian algorithm-configuration research despite the changed title. All 46 pages of v1 and 51 pages of v2, including Appendices A–E, support comparison; relocated proofs and applications can be matched.

before.justification: V1 reports theoretical bounds, proofs, pseudocode and illustrative figures. Statements about empirical success refer to cited research, not original experiments.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical, including its expanded main text and appendices. It reports no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: The Pfaffian GJ operations, linkage formulas, harmonic graph-labeling procedure, logistic objectives and Algorithms 1–2 retain their computational definitions. Expanded explanations and theoretical statements do not introduce a new algorithmic procedure.

E1.justification: Both theoretically analyze clustering, graph-based semi-supervised learning and regularized logistic regression without evaluating datasets. Logistic regression moves from v1 Appendix D.2 to v2 Section 6.3.

E2.justification: Neither version contains an experimentally evaluated comparator set. Comparisons with earlier frameworks concern theoretical guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, budgets or testing procedures. Changes to mathematical assumptions and parameter restrictions concern theorem statements rather than evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical robustness tests, sensitivity studies or error analyses. The revised mathematical illustration and reorganized proofs do not add such analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Probability guarantees and Rademacher complexity concern theoretical analysis.

E6.justification: No measured performance results or qualitative empirical findings are added or revised. Changes to formal guarantees are covered under T1.

T1.justification: V2 adds the general surrogate-transfer guarantee in Lemma 5.6 and reformulates v1's Appendix D.3 complexity result as Theorem 6.5. It corrects Appendix A's Rademacher normalization, revises formal definitions and smoothness premises, and explicitly states f-point-dispersion guarantees. It also omits v1's positive, bounded parameter restriction for online M3, although the retained proof uses it. These are localized revisions around unchanged central Pfaffian and application bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the Pfaffian GJ framework, structured distributional guarantees, dispersion verification and the same three application families. The title change and revised wording do not establish a new core contribution.

C2.justification: V2 discusses general-position and degenerate hypersurfaces in Theorem 7.2 and explains why online analysis requires control of discontinuity locations beyond distributional sign-pattern counting. It also qualifies comparisons with prior bounds as limitations of naive application.

D1.justification: The approximation pseudocode in Algorithms 1–2 is retained, with relocation and repacking. Neither version supplies new implementation resources, hardware information, code availability or experimental reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works are retained after matching author-year and bibliographic updates. V2 corrects the piecewise-framework attribution in Section 2 and more carefully positions its approach as a concrete Pfaffian specialization that avoids difficult dual-class analysis and potentially loose naive applications.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes and rewrites the exposition: it changes the title, expands Section 5.3, moves logistic regression into Section 6.3, restructures Section 7 and brings numerous appendix proofs into the main text. Added proof overviews, subsection headings and author-year citations further change the reading structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced by two plotted views with explicit formulas: seven regions and four piece forms replace the earlier six-region, three-form schematic. Figure 2 remains substantially unchanged, while Algorithms 1–2 are placed together and surrounding material is reflowed.

improvement.justification: V2 offers clearer organization, more explicit theoretical connections, corrected Rademacher normalization and a more concrete Figure 1. However, new Lemma 5.6 compares an empirical minimizer with a population supremum, and Theorem 6.5 likewise uses a supremum for a loss-minimization guarantee. V2 also drops the explicit online M3 parameter restriction still needed by its proof. These mathematical inconsistencies coexist with substantial explanatory gains, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
